bills.title: Cannabis Conviction Clearance Act
bills.summary: Requires every law enforcement agency to seal arrest and conviction records for cannabis possession under CCC 12-410, and under equivalent local charge codes, for offenses dated before January 1, 2024. Sealed records are excluded from court data exports and public records reports and remain visible only to authorized court users, with every access audited; each agency must report how many records it sealed within 30 days after the effective date.

sections.heading: Short title
sections.text: This act may be cited as the Cannabis Conviction Clearance Act.

sections.heading: Sealing of records
sections.text: Arrest and conviction records for possession under Cascadia Criminal Code (CCC) 12-410 with an offense date before January 1, 2024, shall be sealed by every law enforcement agency in the state no later than the effective date of this act.

sections.heading: Effect of sealing
sections.text: Sealed records shall be excluded from court data exports and from public records reports. A sealed record shall remain visible only to authorized court users, and each access to a sealed record shall be recorded in an audit trail.

sections.heading: Local equivalent charge codes
sections.text: Records charged under a local ordinance or county code that is equivalent to CCC 12-410, as mapped by each jurisdiction, are covered by this act to the same extent as records charged under CCC 12-410.

sections.heading: Reporting
sections.text: Within 30 days after the effective date, each law enforcement agency shall report to the State Court Administrator the number of records it sealed under this act.

bills.title: Fireworks Permit Fees
bills.summary: Caps the fees cities and counties may charge for consumer fireworks sales permits and public display permits, waives display fees for nonprofit and local government sponsors, and limits how the fee revenue may be spent.

history.action: Public hearing in House Local Government

sections.heading: Retail sales permits
sections.text: A city, town, or county that requires a permit for the retail sale of consumer fireworks may not charge more than $250 per sales location for each permit season.

sections.heading: Public display permits
sections.text: The fee for a permit to conduct a public fireworks display may not exceed $400 per display. No fee may be charged for a display sponsored by a nonprofit organization or a unit of local government.

sections.heading: Use of fee revenue
sections.text: Permit fee revenue may be used only for fire safety inspections of sales locations and display sites, fireworks safety education, and the cost of issuing permits.

sections.heading: Effective date
sections.text: This act takes effect January 1, 2027.

bills.title: School-Zone Speed Limits
bills.summary: Sets a 20 mph speed limit in school zones when children are present or warning beacons are flashing, defines how far each zone extends, and requires road authorities to post signs marking every zone.

sections.heading: School speed zones
sections.text: The maximum speed in a school speed zone is 20 miles per hour when children are present or when a school zone warning beacon is flashing.

sections.heading: Zone limits
sections.text: A school speed zone extends 300 feet in each direction from the boundary of school grounds along any public road that borders a public or private school.

sections.heading: Signs and beacons
sections.text: Each road authority shall post signs marking the beginning and end of every school speed zone under its jurisdiction and may install warning beacons that operate only during posted school hours.

sections.heading: Effective date
sections.text: This act takes effect July 1, 2027.

bills.title: State Park Day-Use Fee
bills.summary: Sets a $10 per-vehicle day-use fee and a $45 annual pass for state parks, keeps entry free on the first Saturday of each month and for school field trips, and dedicates the revenue to park maintenance.

history.action: Referred to House Natural Resources & Parks

sections.heading: Day-use fee
sections.text: The Department of Parks and Recreation shall charge a day-use fee of $10 per vehicle for entry to any state park that offers day-use facilities.

sections.heading: Annual pass
sections.text: The department shall offer an annual day-use pass for $45, valid at every state park for twelve months from the date of purchase.

sections.heading: Free entry
sections.text: No day-use fee is required on the first Saturday of each month, for school field trips, or for vehicles displaying a disabled veteran license plate.

sections.heading: Use of revenue
sections.text: Day-use fee revenue shall be deposited in the State Parks Maintenance Account and used for trails, restrooms, and visitor facilities.

sections.heading: Effective date
sections.text: This act takes effect January 1, 2027.

bills.title: Rural Broadband Grants
bills.summary: Creates a competitive grant program to extend high-speed internet to unserved and underserved rural areas, sets minimum service speeds for funded projects, and requires a local funding match.

history.action: Referred to House Technology & Economic Development
Public hearing in House Technology & Economic Development

sections.heading: Grant program
sections.text: The Department of Commerce shall establish a competitive grant program to extend high-speed internet service to unserved and underserved rural areas of the state.

sections.heading: Eligible applicants
sections.text: Counties, cities, tribes, public utility districts, port districts, and nonprofit cooperatives may apply for grants under this act.

sections.heading: Service standards
sections.text: Each funded project must provide download speeds of at least 100 megabits per second and upload speeds of at least 20 megabits per second to every location it serves.

sections.heading: Local match
sections.text: A grant may not exceed 75 percent of total project cost, except that the department may waive the match for projects in economically distressed counties.

sections.heading: Effective date
sections.text: This act takes effect July 1, 2027.

bills.title: Fishing License Renewals
bills.summary: Lets anglers renew recreational fishing licenses online or by phone, adds an opt-in automatic renewal with an advance reminder, and creates a 15-day grace period with no late fee.

history.action: Referred to Senate Natural Resources & Wildlife

sections.heading: Online and phone renewal
sections.text: The Department of Fish and Wildlife shall allow a recreational fishing license to be renewed online or by phone at any time during the 60 days before it expires.

sections.heading: Automatic renewal
sections.text: A license holder may choose automatic annual renewal. The department shall send a reminder at least 30 days before each automatic renewal is charged.

sections.heading: Grace period
sections.text: A license renewed within 15 days after it expires is treated as continuously valid, and no late fee may be charged during that period.

sections.heading: Effective date
sections.text: This act takes effect March 1, 2027.

bills.title: Daylight Saving Study
bills.summary: Creates a temporary task force to compare permanent standard time with permanent daylight saving time and deliver recommendations to the legislature by December 1, 2027.

history.action: Public hearing in House State Government

sections.heading: Task force created
sections.text: A seven-member task force on daylight saving time is created. The governor shall appoint members representing agriculture, schools, public health, transportation, and small business.

sections.heading: Scope of study
sections.text: The task force shall compare remaining on standard time year-round with observing daylight saving time year-round, including effects on sleep, traffic safety, energy use, and coordination with neighboring states.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.text: The task force shall deliver its findings and recommendations to the legislature by December 1, 2027, and expires on that date.

sections.heading: Effective date
sections.text: This act takes effect upon enactment.

bills.title: Wildfire Smoke Alerts
bills.summary: Requires the Department of Health to issue county-level wildfire smoke alerts when fine-particle air pollution is forecast to reach unhealthy levels, and sets protective steps for schools and outdoor workers while an alert is in effect.

history.action: Referred to Senate Health & Human Services
Public hearing in Senate Health & Human Services

sections.heading: Smoke alerts
sections.text: The Department of Health shall issue a wildfire smoke alert for each county where the air quality index for fine particulate matter is forecast to exceed 150.

sections.heading: Alert delivery
sections.text: Alerts shall be sent through the state emergency notification system and broadcast media, posted on the department's website, and made available in the five languages most commonly spoken in each affected county.

sections.heading: Schools and outdoor workers
sections.text: While an alert is in effect, school districts in the affected county shall move recess and athletics indoors, and employers shall provide approved respirators to employees who work outdoors.

sections.heading: Effective date
sections.text: This act takes effect June 1, 2027.
